key_insight: In a very large US screening mammography cohort, commercial AI CAD tools showed meaningful performance differences, with algorithm D performing best overall and the open-source model Mirai performing similarly to two commercial products.
clinical_relevance: The study supports local validation before deploying mammography AI, because the best choice depends on the intended workflow and threshold, not just FDA clearance.
method: Analyzed 707,922 screening mammograms with complete data from 2022–2023.
Applied three FDA-cleared commercial AI algorithms plus the open-source Mirai model to standard screening views.
Compared AUROC and operating-point performance using matched AI-positive rates; cancer outcomes were linked through registry data.
evidence_signal: Performance was evaluated against 12-month cancer ascertainment, with algorithm D achieving the highest AUROC (0.849) and the highest sensitivity across AI-positive thresholds.
watch_item: Results come from one health system and show that no algorithm matched radiologist sensitivity at AI-positive rates of 10% or less, so real-world deployment still needs careful threshold selection and local testing.
paper_title: Kaiser Permanente National Cross-Vendor Validation of Mammography Artificial Intelligence Computer-Aided Diagnosis Algorithms in a US-Representative Population
